correctness.rationale: The product formula for cube heat kernels makes B(x,y)=b(x xor y). The squared entrywise kernel W has Walsh eigenvalues Lambda_r given by double integral A(s,t)^{d-r}D(s,t)^r, where A=(1+e^{-2(s+t)})/2, D=(e^{-2s}+e^{-2t})/2 and A-D=(1-e^{-2s})(1-e^{-2t})/2. Since the finite positive mixing measure gives positive mass to (0,infty), Lambda_0>...>Lambda_d>0. Independence and Rademacher fourth moment produce Var=N(Lambda_0-2w(0))+sigma^T W sigma. Walsh Parseval then gives the exact nonnegative excess sum and unique equality when sigma is ± top-degree parity character. Independently constructed rational Green kernel for d=3,B=(I+L)^-1 and enumerated all 256 sign maps, finding optimum 1024/3675 attained exactly twice. This finite check corroborates, but does not replace, the all-d/full-measure proof.
residual_risks: The theorem optimizes variance only, with one probe per color, not fixed computational cost or tail risk.

value.rationale: A unique globally minimum-variance partition is a natural optimization invariant for the widely used stochastic trace estimator on the hypercube, not a relabeling of a generic formula. The all-positive-heat-mixture assertion and exact spectral gap quantify robustness to every competing two-coloring and are useful for designing stochastic probes, including resolvent kernels.
residual_risks: Does not claim speedup at equal computational cost across different probe counts.

final_claim: For any d>=1 and nontrivial finite positive heat-mixture kernel B on the Boolean cube, the parity bipartition is the unique (up to swapping labels) global minimum-variance two-color Rademacher trace probing partition, with exact Walsh spectral excess-variance identity for all sign assignments.
limitations: Nontrivial positive finite measure is required; at t=0-only the optimum is not unique.
No confidence statement about arbitrary signed mixtures or graph families beyond cubes.
